proposals.title: Implement nominal types and scale constants in packages/core
proposals.why_now: CanonicalEncoder is the only substantive code in packages/core. ADR-003 is TRAVADO and fully specifies Money, Quantity, Price, Rate as branded bigint types and Tick as a branded safe-integer number with validation. No DEFINIR decision blocks these definitions — scale constants (QUANTITY_SCALE, PRICE_SCALE, RATE_SCALE), constructor-validators, and overflow guards are all precisely specified. Every downstream FASE-1 package (domain, world, application, contracts) is blocked at the type level until these exist. This is the shallowest FASE-1 dependency with the widest fan-out and zero open decisions required.

proposals.title: Write ADR-002 and implement deterministic positional RNG in packages/core
proposals.why_now: ADR-002 is TRAVADO and requires the hash function to be specified bit-by-bit in an ADR before any rand() implementation. The spec recommends SplitMix64 over FNV-1a and lists the hash function as an open DEFINIR in §19. INV-02 — described explicitly as the most important test of the project — requires that price(asset, t) consulted directly equals the result of advancing tick by tick, which is only possible with a stateless positional RNG. All six world namespaces (market.trend, market.factor, market.regime, macro.schedule, bot.policy, bot.decision) are blocked until rand() exists.

proposals.title: Write ADR-004 and implement bigint division helpers in packages/core
proposals.why_now: ADR-004 is TRAVADO: every operation that loses precision must declare its rounding mode explicitly, and calling division without a mode must be a compile-time or lint-blocking error. The enforcement mechanism is the open DEFINIR. Without the three helpers (TRUNCATE_TOWARD_ZERO, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_HALF_EVEN) and their lint guard, the domain ledger cannot implement spot execution, fee calculation, notional computation, or rounding residue posting (INV-07). Implementing the ledger before this is in place allows implicit division to proliferate in domain code unchecked.

proposals.title: Implement domain double-entry ledger in packages/domain
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires 'Ledger multi-commodity de dupla entrada' and 'Ordem a mercado, compra e venda spot'. INV-04, INV-05, and INV-06 are FASE-1 acceptance gate invariants that cannot be satisfied without this. The ledger is a prerequisite for every domain operation — spot buy, sell, fee posting, rounding residue — and must exist before the tick loop and StateHash can be implemented. Once IDEA-001 (nominal types) and IDEA-003 (division helpers) are merged, no DEFINIR blocks ledger implementation since the account structure, transaction format, causationId requirement, and per-commodity zero-sum rule are all fully specified.

repository_assessment.current_state: Infrastructure and tooling are complete: monorepo skeleton, TypeScript strict mode, determinism lint (all §13 rules active and tested), dependency boundary checker (§14.5 graph enforced), workspace configuration, and CanonicalEncoder with ADR-009 accepted and tested (over 100 tests). One ADR is on file. Every other package — world, domain, application, narrative, contracts, adapters, ui, and all apps/desktop sub-packages — is an empty stub exporting nothing. No nominal types, no positional RNG, no division helpers, no ledger, no price generator, no tick loop, no save system, no CLI replay tool, no benchmark tool, no minimal UI, and no installer exist. Checkpoints 0034 through 0041 all report NO_ACCEPTED_CHANGES.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: packages/core is missing the foundational nominal integer types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, Tick) specified by ADR-003 TRAVADO. These have no open DEFINIR decisions, no ambiguity, and no dependencies. Until they exist, packages/domain, packages/world, and packages/application cannot be implemented at the type level. This is the shallowest dependency node with the widest FASE-1 fan-out.

warnings: 41 consecutive checkpoints (0001–0041) report NO_ACCEPTED_CHANGES after the canonical encoder was implemented. The same five proposals have been generated in every cycle from CYCLE-000070 onward. The block is not in the analysis — the repository state is genuinely unchanged. If proposals continue to be generated without acceptance, the bottleneck is in the Builder or Reviewer role.

Three open DEFINIR decisions block distinct FASE-1 work streams simultaneously: (a) hash function algorithm for ADR-002, which blocks rand() and every world namespace consumer; (b) technical enforcement mechanism for division rounding mode (ADR-004), which blocks ledger fee and notional calculation; (c) fixed-point or lookup-table strategy for log-space price construction plus octave parameters (§5.1), which blocks the price generator. These should be resolved in parallel rather than sequentially to avoid compressing the FASE-1 critical path.

FASE-1 acceptance requires a minimum installer for Windows and Linux (§14.6 TRAVADO). The spec warns explicitly that deferring this risks discovering ABI failures, native module rebuild issues, and path errors in the final week with no time to correct architecture. No Electron code, no electron-builder configuration, and no INV-29 compliance audit exist after 41 checkpoints. This risk grows every cycle this is postponed.
